title: Stage 68 external-source provenance ledger
inspection_scope: Freshly downloaded current arXiv v1 PDFs for the three 2026 preprints listed below and checked theorem statements and cited dependencies relevant to this report. This is not a line-by-line proof audit. Other sources and the OpenAI manuscript remain inherited from Stage 64.

sources.title: Fourth moments of prime exponential sums and exceptional sets for sums and differences of primes
hypotheses: Q_Theta: every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet L-function has real part at most fixed Theta, with 1/2 <= Theta; Theorem 1 establishes the stated range Theta < 11/12
fixed smooth Gevrey prime weight w, with 0 <= w <= 1 and w=1 on [1/8,7/8]
major rational cores with P=X^kappa and fixed kappa in the paper's stated range; arcs are disjoint for sufficiently large X
relevant_conclusions: global minor fourth moment is O(X^(5/2)(log X)^100) under the theorem's hypotheses
Theorem 2 exceptional-set estimate is O(X^(1/2)(log X)^100)
Proposition 4.1 gives a uniform major-coefficient asymptotic with positive real main term for even N in [X/2,X], under its stated assumptions
sources.stage68_relevance: These are global moment and major-arc/exceptional-set statements. They do not state a target-uniform signed minor coefficient or the required localized increment-energy estimate.
sources.local_copy: Downloaded during Stage 68 to temporary storage; no repository PDF added.

sources.title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
hypotheses: Theorem 1 uses a common zero-free half-plane for all Dirichlet L-functions and the paper's explicit-formula/prime-exponential-sum inputs
Theorem 3's H_theta range is 1/2 <= theta <= 2/3 and uses the paper's stated classical fixed-modulus zero-density inputs
relevant_conclusions: Theorem 3 gives exponent g(theta)=theta(5-4theta)/(2(2-theta)) in its stated range
sources.stage68_relevance: Positive-power exceptional-set estimates permit isolated targets; neither result is the requested signed bound at every prescribed N.
sources.local_copy: Downloaded during Stage 68 to temporary storage; no repository PDF added.

sources.authors: I. Althöfer, D. Chen, A. Perelli, and J. Pintz
sources.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers among polynomial values
hypotheses: fixed integer polynomial of positive leading coefficient and degree k >= 2
imports the upstream Li-Liu results and cites the OpenAI manuscript for one input
relevant_conclusions: exceptional indices along 2 phi(n) are O_(phi,epsilon)(N^(alpha_k+epsilon)); alpha_2=1/2, alpha_3=5/8, alpha_4=3/4, and alpha_k=1-1/(k+1) for k>=5
sources.stage68_relevance: A sparse polynomial subsequence result does not cover all even integers, and the exceptional-index power bound does not imply zero exceptions.
sources.local_copy: Downloaded during Stage 68 to temporary storage; no repository PDF added.
